actions: Pinned and validated the public second-corpus repository noureddinekhender-alt/judge-human-agreement at commit 63b98c57426742d19169af0dc7ec9f888f928d8c.
Verified current-main README, judge-call schema, human error threshold/common-set logic, prompt-intervention table, individual judge kappas, and naive ensemble table from exact-ref primary artifacts.
Corrected the experiment scope: this corpus has same-model alternate-prompt calls rather than same-prompt stochastic repeats.
Wrote a deterministic train/test, train-only-selection, call-count-matched second-corpus routing protocol without executing unmounted public bytes.
Performed a breadth repair with primary-source scans of AgentConductor dynamic topology and SAGE self-evolution.
material_findings: On the pinned 147-item common set, the six-judge majority-vote kappa is 0.401, below the best single v1 judge at 0.534 and the second-best at 0.515; raw judge count is not a safe optimization target.
Same-model v2 prompt intervention can improve or sharply degrade agreement depending on judge, so it must not be treated as an iid repeat.
AgentConductor reports difficulty-conditioned dynamic topology with up to +14.6% pass@1, -13% density, and -68% token cost in its tested code settings.
SAGE reports four-role self-evolution with external verification and +8.9% LiveCodeBench / +10.7% OlympiadBench for Qwen-2.5-7B; component effects remain unresolved.
blocker: The connected GitHub corpus can be inspected through the connector but its large raw CSV bytes cannot currently be mounted into the local Python runtime, while outbound Python/container network access is unavailable. Therefore the held-out second-corpus routing script was not executed and no quantitative test result was invented.
termination: Invocation checkpointed under the frozen semantic tuple after useful public-source/protocol progress; recurring research is not globally complete.
exact_next_action: At the next invocation, freeze the then-current control tuple first.
